title: Controlled RFC 2198 recovery into a real WebRTC T.140 data channel
objective: Prove that an omitted RFC 4103 T.140 generation can be reconstructed from RFC 2198 redundancy at the media-terminating gateway and delivered exactly once over a real WebRTC t140 data channel while preserving the degraded SIP-side packet evidence.

securityModel.rule: The gateway inspects RFC 4103/RFC 2198 media, reconstructs missing T.140, and re-originates content on WebRTC. Per-leg encryption does not establish end-to-end encryption across this gateway.

runnableEvidence: RttSipProbe declares a sender-controlled omission of RTP sequence 1 carrying B
the gateway receives sequence 0 and sequence 2 but never receives sequence 1
sequence 2 carries one RFC 2198 redundant generation representing the missing B plus current primary C
the gateway forwards the two received RTP datagrams byte-for-byte unchanged to the SIP-side interpreter receiver
the gateway emits A from sequence 0, reconstructs B from the redundant generation, then emits current primary C
the gateway records the source of every emitted block as primary, redundant, or missing-marker
a real Chromium RTCPeerConnection receives A, B, C on an ordered reliable t140 data channel
Python independently applies Baudot's RFC 4103 recovery reducer to the preserved packets and requires the same A + B + C result
requiredBeforeProven: network-induced loss in a routed substrate rather than sender-controlled omission
multiple consecutive losses with sufficient and insufficient redundancy
out-of-order arrival policy and timer behavior
at least one additional independent WebRTC implementation
production-representative VRS or gateway observations without provider-specific reducer branches

doesNotEstablish: end-to-end encryption across the media-terminating gateway
